bullets: How to find the mean, median and mode of a data set, build a cumulative frequency table for grouped data, draw the ogive, and read the median and interquartile range off it
slides.heading: Secondary E-math: statistics — mean, median, mode and the ogive
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we summarise data three ways, watch one extreme score pull the mean around, then build a curve that lets us read off medians and quartiles.

bullets: Calculate the mean, median and mode, and choose which centre describes a data set honestly
Build a cumulative frequency table, draw the ogive and read off the median, quartiles and interquartile range
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the goals aloud and tell the class: keep these in mind, because the exit ticket at the end will ask you to do exactly these things.

bullets: Nine test scores have mean 10 - if the top score jumps from 18 to 27, what happens to the mean?
Does the middle score move too, or does it stay put?
slides.heading: One score of 27 - does the centre move?
slides.notes: Ask for predictions and take two or three answers without judging them yet; say: the scenes will move the outlier and watch which centre chases it.

bullets: Mean = total divided by count; median = the middle value; mode = the most frequent value
For grouped data, plot cumulative frequency against the upper class boundaries to get the ogive, and read centres off it
slides.heading: Three centres and one climbing curve
slides.notes: Say this slowly, because it is the map for the whole lesson: first three ways to name a centre, then a table and a curve for data that arrives in groups.

bullets: Each of the nine scores drops onto the number line as one dot: 5, 7, 8, 8, 9, 10, 11, 14, 18
The total is 90, so the mean marker slides in at 90 / 9 = 10
slides.heading: Nine scores, one dot each
slides.notes: Narrate the scene as it plays: count the dots as they land, add them up together, then watch the mean marker slide to the fair-share position at 10.

bullets: The mean marker travels to 10, the total shared equally among the nine scores
The median ring settles on the fifth dot, 9, and the mode bar grows tallest under 8, which appears twice
slides.heading: Three centres: mean 10, median 9, mode 8
slides.notes: Narrate the scene as it plays: three different markers find three different centres on the same nine dots - mean 10, median 9, mode 8.

bullets: Drag the top score from 18 up to 27: the total becomes 99 and the mean chases it up to 11
The median ring never moves: the middle of the list is still 9
slides.heading: The mean follows the outlier; the median resists
slides.notes: Narrate the scene as it plays: one dot travels a long way, the mean marker follows it, and the median ring stays exactly where it was.

bullets: Each class is represented by its midpoint: the f x column totals 600 over 24 values
The cumulative frequency column climbs 2, 8, 16, 22, 24 as the frequencies pile up
slides.heading: Grouped data: the cumulative frequency table
slides.notes: Narrate the scene as it plays: row by row the midpoint stands in for its class, the f x products accumulate to 600, and the cumulative column grows beside them.

bullets: Plot each upper class boundary - 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 - against its cumulative frequency
The probe walks the points 2, 8, 16, 22, 24 and the S-shaped curve draws itself behind it
slides.heading: The ogive: cumulative frequency curve
slides.notes: Narrate the scene as it plays: the table turns into a curve, each point one class higher and one cumulative total further along.

bullets: Half of 24 is 12: run across from 12 to the curve, then drop down - the median is about 25
The same read-off from 6 and 18 gives quartiles about 16.7 and 33.3, so the IQR is about 16.7
slides.heading: Read-off: median ≈ 25, IQR ≈ 16.7
slides.notes: Narrate the scene as it plays: the dashed line grows across to the curve and drops to the marks axis three times - once for the median and once for each quartile.

bullets: The beam of scores balances only with the fulcrum under 10, the mean
The tallest bar is the mode, 8 - a different centre that answers a different question
slides.heading: The mean is the balance point, not the tallest bar
slides.notes: Narrate the scene as it plays: slide the fulcrum along the beam until it balances at 10, and notice the tallest bar sitting somewhere else entirely.

bullets: Estimated mean = total of f x over total frequency = 600 / 24 = 25
Each value was replaced by its class midpoint, so 25 is an estimate, not an exact mean
slides.heading: Worked example: estimating the mean from the table
slides.notes: Work this on the board slowly: list the midpoints, multiply, add, divide - and stress the word estimate, because the raw values inside each class are unknown.

bullets: Find the mean, median and mode of 4, 6, 7, 7, 9, 12, 15
Then open the worksheet: one outlier question, one grouped-table question and one ogive read-off
slides.heading: Your turn
slides.notes: Give three quiet minutes for the first task, take the three centres from the class, then set the worksheet going in pairs.

bullets: Four questions: the outlier and the two centres, the new mean, the interquartile range, and a cumulative frequency
Write one sentence: when an outlier is present, which centre do you report, and why?
slides.heading: Exit ticket
slides.notes: Collect the tickets at the door; the first question revisits the trap from the last scene, so it shows straight away who can choose a centre honestly.
